oliver: Trying to get the TS sample for an edge worker running. Hitting a weird overload + runtime mismatch when importing the JS SDK in an edge bundle.

oliver: Repro: in worker: `const c = createClient({ apiKey: Deno.env.get('KEY') }); await c.chat.generate({ model: 'gpt-lite', input: 'hi' });`

oliver: tsc error: `No overload matches this call. Argument of type '{ model: string; input: string; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'GenerateOptions'. Property 'input' is incompatible.' Runtime then fails with `TypeError: node stream async iterator not implemented` if I bundle without forcing the /edge entry.

maya: Two layers: (1) d.ts overload ordering where streaming signature precedes simple signature so TS picks wrong overload; (2) package exports/bundler resolving to node entry pulling in node stream code.

liam: What do your tsconfig and package.json show? Edge libs affect DOM types and ReadableStream vs NodeStream conflicts.

oliver: tsconfig has lib ["ES2021","WebWorker"], moduleResolution bundler, strict true. package.json has "type":"module".

julia: Quick fixes: (A) explicitly import `redwood-inference/edge` in samples to force edge build, (B) call `client.chat.generate<string>(...)` to satisfy TS. Both are ok for docs but not ideal UX.

sam: SDK-side: reorder overloads so non-streaming call appears first. Also add `./edge` types export so TS resolves edge shapes. Consider adding a `runtime?: 'edge' | 'node'` discriminant to GenerateOptions to make inference deterministic.

maya: For onboarding we debated using `T = any` for sample wrappers to avoid forcing explicit generics. Core lib keeps `T = unknown` for strictness. Could also export a `createLooseClient()` for examples.

julia: Also document tsconfig hints: include WebWorker lib, `moduleResolution: 'bundler'`, and note `package.json` type module. Add short troubleshooting note: if you see stream runtime error, import `/edge`.

devx-bot: Filed DEVEX-1009: typing + edge export follow-up. Proposed small PR: (1) overload reorder, (2) edge.d.ts export, (3) createEdgeAdapter({fetch}) helper.

oliver: Thanks all. Will try the patched sample with explicit import and report back. :thumbsup:
